questions.q: According to this lesson, what does an agent framework actually add on top of the raw tool-use mechanism from Lesson 3?
options: A completely different, incompatible way for models to call tools
Nothing — frameworks and the raw API are functionally identical with no differences
A guarantee that the agent will never make a mistake
Conveniences like the loop itself, state management, retries, and multi-agent coordination — it wraps the mechanism, not replaces it
questions.explain: A framework saves you from rewriting the same hard parts (looping, state, retries, coordination) on every project, but the underlying tool-use mechanism is the same one covered in Lesson 3.

questions.q: How does the Claude Agent SDK position itself, per this lesson?
options: As a vendor-neutral abstraction layer that works identically across every LLM provider
As a purely visual, no-code drag-and-drop tool
As the same agent loop, built-in tools, and context management that power Claude Code, available as a library
As a framework with no support for tool use at all
questions.explain: It's Anthropic's own answer to using Claude Code's agent loop inside your own application, installable via npm or pip.

questions.q: What distinguishes LangGraph's approach from CrewAI's, according to this lesson?
options: LangGraph has no concept of state, while CrewAI tracks all state automatically
They are functionally identical with different names
LangGraph uses explicit, low-level graph control (nodes and edges you define); CrewAI uses a faster-to-stand-up, role-based 'crew' model with less granular control
CrewAI requires writing raw JSON Schema by hand, while LangGraph does not
questions.explain: LangGraph leans toward explicit, controllable orchestration for complex production workflows; CrewAI optimizes for quickly standing up a working multi-agent system.

questions.q: What happened to the original AutoGen project in October 2025, and what carries its ideas forward now?
options: AutoGen was deleted entirely with no successor
Microsoft moved AutoGen into maintenance mode; AG2 (a community fork) and Microsoft Agent Framework (the official successor) now carry the idea forward
AutoGen was renamed to LangGraph
Nothing changed — AutoGen remains the actively developed flagship project
questions.explain: Microsoft placed AutoGen in maintenance mode in October 2025; AG2 is the active community fork by its original creators, and Microsoft Agent Framework is Microsoft's official successor merging AutoGen and Semantic Kernel.

questions.q: Why does this course teach agent concepts using the raw Claude API directly instead of picking one framework to standardize on?
options: Because the underlying concepts transfer to any framework a real job might use, while framework-specific API calls don't transfer back the other way
Because none of the frameworks mentioned actually work in production
Because frameworks cannot call tools at all
Because this course considers frameworks obsolete and never worth learning
questions.explain: Learning the loop, schemas, routing, and multi-agent patterns at the mechanism level means the knowledge applies regardless of which framework (or none) a given job happens to use.
